function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Practical Tips | |-------|---------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits: 35–55 mph on rural roads, 45–65 mph on highways, 25–35 mph in residential zones.
• “No speed limit” zones exist in some rural areas; drivers must use common sense. | • Always obey posted signs; use a GPS that updates speed limits. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• The law applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles (helmet required). | • Check the seat‑belt sign on your dashboard; it turns green when all occupants are buckled. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held texting or calling is illegal while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• “Text‑while‑driving” is a moving‑violation offense. | • Use voice‑activated commands or a Bluetooth headset. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02 % BAC).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | • Designate a sober driver or use rideshare services if you’ve been drinking. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights. | • Always check for pedestrians and cyclists before proceeding. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• The bus’s stop sign must be extended. | • Do not pass a stopped school bus until the sign is retracted. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Overtake only when safe and legal. | • Keep a safe following distance (at least 2 seconds). | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, 15 ft of a stop sign, or 30 ft of a railroad crossing.
• Parking on a curb is prohibited unless marked. | • Pay attention to “No Parking” signs and street‑cleaning schedules. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing a vehicle requires a proper tow‑bar and a towing permit if the vehicle is not registered. | • Keep your registration and insurance documents in the glove compartment. | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Texas uses automated speed cameras and red‑light cameras in many cities. | • Drive within posted limits and obey traffic signals to avoid fines. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles: helmet required for riders under 18; no seat belt.
• Commercial vehicles: must follow specific weight and size regulations. | • If you operate a commercial vehicle, ensure you’re familiar with the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) regulations. | ### Quick Reference Resources - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Official traffic law handbook and driver’s manual. - **TxDOT** – Highway safety statistics and enforcement updates. - **Texas Legislature Online** – Current statutes and amendments. - **Local County Courts** – Information on traffic citations and penalties. --- **Tip:** If you’re planning to drive in Texas, download a reliable GPS app that updates speed limits and traffic camera locations. This can help you stay compliant and avoid unexpected fines.
